decision.summary: Brush-up is not a v1 release blocker. Brush-up-specific provider, cleanup, retention, revoke, deletion, cost, latency, retry, and script-scoped feasibility requirements move to v1.1 entry criteria.

deferredFromV1: Brush-up generated audio candidate acceptance flow
Brush-up-specific cost, latency, and retry proof
keptInV1: App-owned Storage and protected replay for existing generated audio and recordings
Privacy, consent, support, and account deletion readiness for the actual v1 feature set
Provider kill switch gap closure for v1 providers
Store assets, release QA, closed testing, submission, and rejection-fix loop

gate3_5Redefinition.oldMeaning: Brush-up MVP implementation / revoke-delete proof if Brush-up remained v1 scope
gate3_5Redefinition.newMeaning: v1 core readiness and release-scope cleanup before native packaging
scope: Confirm Brush-up is hidden, not implemented, and not marketed as v1 functionality
Close or explicitly accept remaining v1 provider kill switch gaps
Confirm normal v1 provider surfaces have safe failure and support paths
Confirm privacy, deletion, and consent claims match the v1 feature set without Brush-up
Park Brush-up v1.1 requirements with owners and entry criteria
Decide whether remaining Gate 3 WARN items block Gate 4 or move to Gate 6 release QA

v1_1BrushUpEntryCriteria: ElevenLabs supports the chosen script-scoped best-take-to-voice-material approach.
ElevenLabs delete and cleanup semantics are known for normal cloned voices and script-scoped Brush-up material/variants.
ElevenLabs retention and deletion semantics are known enough for consent, revoke, Privacy Policy, Data Safety, and account deletion claims.
Brush-up cost, latency, and retry behavior is understood enough to decide whether Vercel Route Handlers remain sufficient.
NATIVE_MINUTE_DISABLE_ELEVENLABS env presence and safe operation proof are recorded.
Account deletion proof covers Brush-up material, provider variants, generated Brush-up audio, saved pins, app-owned Storage, DB rows, and provider cleanup.
Protected replay proof covers Brush-up generated audio and does not rely on provider direct URLs.
Brush-up consent and revoke copy are finalized before best take audio is sent to a provider as voice material.
notes: Existing voice, clone voice, and Brush-up architecture documents are retained as future planning inputs.
Brush-up does not block Gate 4 if it remains non-user-facing and absent from v1 Store metadata.
No secrets, env values, raw provider responses, transcript body, private audio paths, provider identifiers, or billing details are recorded.
